## TL;DR

The macOS Hub CI job was red because `HubFindBarContainerTests.testHidingFindBarReturnsFocusToThePage` crashed at teardown (XCTMemoryChecker), not because the focus assertion failed. The test now uses the same window teardown pattern as other Hub window tests, strict first-responder checks aligned with production (`window.firstResponder === webView`), and a precise pre-condition via `findBarOwnsFocus` (not `containsKeyboardFocus`, which false-passes when focus stays anywhere in the container). Swift 6 concurrency warnings in `LocalServerDiscoveryTests` were cleaned up with `OSAllocatedUnfairLock`. Local `xcodebuild test` for the find-bar case passed (~0.56 s). GitHub Actions on `main` was not re-run from this session.

## Work and rationale

GitHub Actions run 41769376401 and earlier runs only surfaced the test name with a 0.000 s duration. Inspecting failed logs and a local xcresult showed XCTest’s memory checker aborting after the test body when a `WKWebView` lived in an `NSWindow` without orderly teardown. `HubWorkspaceChromeTests` already set `isReleasedWhenClosed = false`, drain the run loop, nil out `contentView`, then close; this test now matches that pattern so CI does not confuse a checker crash with a failed assertion.

The product behavior under test is unchanged: when the find bar held focus, `hideFindInterface()` schedules `window.makeFirstResponder(webView)` on the main queue (#0789). The test must prove that handoff, not merely that keyboard focus is “somewhere” in the container. `containsKeyboardFocus(in:)` intentionally treats the whole container (including the hidden find bar subtree and the shared field editor host) as in-scope for menu validation, so using it in this regression test would pass even if focus never moved to the web view. Review pass 1 called that out; assertions now mirror `HubServerWebContainerView.findBarOwnsFocus` for the pre-hide check and identity-compare `window.firstResponder` to `container.webView` after polling through the async handoff.

Supporting changes: `settleFocusWindow` runs layout and short run-loop slices so AppKit can install the field editor after `makeKeyAndOrderFront` and `presentFindInterface`. `LocalServerDiscoveryTests` replaced `NSLock` and a captured `var` in an `onUpdate` closure with `OSAllocatedUnfairLock`-backed recorders so Swift 6 strict concurrency does not later fail the same job. Documentation in `docs/macos-hub-release.md` records the CI symptom, root cause, and fix for future triage.

## Approaches tried

An intermediate version relaxed post-hide checks to `containsKeyboardFocus(in: window)` to get green locally while fixing teardown. Review correctly rejected that as a false-pass guard. The shipped approach keeps teardown hardening and restores strict responder identity, with `findBarOwnsFocus` duplicated in the test target (matching production logic) so pre- and post-conditions stay precise without widening production APIs.

Polling up to one second for `firstResponder === webView` accommodates `DispatchQueue.main.async` in `hideFindInterface()` without a fixed sleep that might flake on slower runners.

## Challenges and blockers

The workflow runs on push to `main` only, so confirming the job green on GitHub requires merge; this session verified the targeted test via local `xcodebuild test` with `CODE_SIGNING_ALLOWED=NO`, mirroring CI’s unsigned test step.

`LocalServerDiscoveryTests` can fail on developer machines when `~/.repoos/servers` registers live ports (port scan skipped, real ports returned). That is environmental, pre-existing, and not what broke CI; hermetic registry injection remains a follow-up suggestion, not part of this task.

## Key learnings

Instant (0.000 s) XCTest failures on headless macOS runners often mean abort at scope exit or memory checking, not a fast assertion miss—always pull `--log-failed` or an xcresult before changing product code.

Focus regression tests for AppKit should assert `firstResponder` identity (or field-editor delegate wiring), not helper methods whose semantics include deliberate permissiveness for menu state elsewhere in the app.
